Reconnect Conflicts & Multi-Writer Design

mtime/hash checks are necessary but not a full design. Remote editing is a multi-writer problem: local buffer cache, remote disk, optional second client, and tools (formatters, builds) may all change the same path.

Version vectors

  • Each file has (path, content_hash, remote_gen, local_gen). Opens fetch hash+gen; every successful write increments remote_gen on agent.
  • Local edits bump local_gen and keep base_hash from last sync.

Write protocol

  1. Client sends FS_WRITE with expected base_hash / remote_gen and new content (or diff).
  2. Agent applies only if current remote matches expectation (compare-and-swap).
  3. Mismatch → Conflict with remote blob (or diff); client does not silently overwrite.

Conflict UX

  • Open 3-way UI: base (last sync) · local · remote; actions: keep local, keep remote, merge buffer.
  • Offline queue: ordered ops; on reconnect replay CAS writes; stop queue on first conflict for that path; continue unrelated paths.
  • External remote edits (another SSH user): watchers update dirty flags; if buffer dirty locally → conflict, else auto-reload with notification.
Important

Last-write-wins by mtime alone is rejected. CAS + explicit conflict UI is required before advertising multi-hour offline remote editing.
